deities: Shiva (as Rudra Mahadev; no active worship now)

history.period: Construction begun c. 943 CE under Mularaja I; completed 1140 CE under Siddharaja Jayasimha
history.summary: This is a temple RUIN, not an active temple. Once one of India's largest Shiva temple complexes (about 91 m by 70 m, 1600 pillars, 12 gateways, 11 shrines of Rudra Mahadev), founded in the 10th century by Solanki founder Mularaja I and completed in 1140 CE by Siddharaja Jayasimha. It was demolished by Alauddin Khilji's forces in 1296 CE and again by Ahmed Shah I in the early 15th century, part being converted into the Jami Masjid. Today only two ornate torana gateways and a few massive carved pillars survive. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds 'Patan', which is the district; the actual town is Siddhpur and the real state is Gujarat. Opening hours and any regular worship unverified.

name: Siddhpur Rudra Mahalaya Temple Site
town_description: Siddhpur (Sristhal) is an ancient pilgrimage town in Patan district on the banks of the Saraswati river, named after the Solanki ruler Siddharaja Jayasimha. It is known for the ruined Rudra Mahalaya, the Bindu Sarovar ritual tank, and the Bohra merchant havelis of its old quarters.
